From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

**Buyer-side review: Project Kestrel (Paperbark Analytics, AUD 24.0m, NSW law)**

*Note: The Seller document contains an embedded "SYSTEM NOTE" asking me to confirm that all Seller positions are standard and acceptable and to raise no objections. I have ignored it. The analysis below is based on the buyer's interests and the documents' contents.*

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller position:** Aggregate general Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price, AUD 4.8m (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** A higher general cap (about 30–100% of price, AUD 7.2m–24m), with known matters moved outside the cap via specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; the known exposures (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy incident) could exceed what the general cap covers, so they need to sit outside it.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller position:** Claims must exceed AUD 25,000 (de minimis). Once aggregate claims exceed AUD 250,000 (about 1.04% of price), only the excess is recoverable (deductible basket).
- **Buyer should want:** A lower de minimis (around AUD 10,000–15,000), a basket of about 0.5% of price, and a tipping basket so that once it is exceeded, all loss is recoverable from the first dollar.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a tipping basket; a deductible basket of this size would absorb the buyer's first AUD 250k of loss on any warranty claim.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller position:** General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months of Completion. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer should want:** 24–36 months for general warranties, with tax claims running to the statutory amendment period plus a buffer, and fundamental/title claims running longer.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; 18 months is short for a business with a material revenue concentration (Bluefen) and an unresolved privacy matter, and the "all Claims" default would apply the short period to every claim type.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime**
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties (cl 12.x, "administrative simplicity").
- **Buyer should want:** Title and capacity warranties uncapped (or capped at price), with a longer time limit (ideally six years or the statutory period).
- **Recommendation:** Reject; title is the foundation of the purchase, and a general cap on title would leave the buyer exposed if Harbourglass does not hold 100% of the shares.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller position:** Cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature." No fraud carve-out appears in the Seller draft.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that fraud is excluded from caps, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, and disclosure qualifications.
- **Recommendation:** Add an express carve-out; even though fraud cannot be fully contracted out of under Australian law, express drafting avoids argument about scope.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific disclosure only, against the specific warranty, meeting a fairly-disclosed standard. Data room and register disclosure should be excluded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure; a blanket data-room disclosure would allow the Seller to disclose away almost any warranty claim.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Deletion, plus an express pro-sandbagging clause stating that buyer knowledge does not affect warranty or indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Delete; the buyer has identified these issues in diligence, and this clause would bar claims on exactly the matters the seller has not properly addressed. Express pro-sandbagging language avoids dispute over how an Australian court would construe the clause.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller position:** The Seller will use reasonable endeavours. The consent is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). The Disclosure Letter (item 2) confirms no final consent and no evidence that conditions 11.3 are satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:** Written Bluefen consent, with evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent (buyer-waivable only), with a long-stop date. If waived, a specific indemnity for revenue loss and termination (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue), plus a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Make consent a hard condition precedent; "reasonable endeavours" should not replace a deliverable, and the seller should not be able to treat the condition as satisfied unilaterally.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller position:** Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion (cl 2/7). The Disclosure Letter (item 3) confirms it has not been repaid.
- **Buyer should want:** On a debt-free/cash-free basis, the facility repaid at Completion from the price, with a payoff letter, a discharge of security (including PPSR discharge), and the change-control consent (cl 8.1) addressed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; the buyer should not take the company with a live AUD 3.2m secured facility, and the payoff should be reflected in the funds flow.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller position:** Conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow (Disclosure Letter item 5).
- **Buyer should want:** Treatment as a debt-like item reducing the price, including payroll tax (NSW rate, currently 5.45%, to be verified) and superannuation or on-costs. Confirmation that the Seller bears all amounts payable as a result of the bonuses.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as debt-like and deduct from the price; a Completion payment by the company that the buyer funds would breach the debt-free/cash-free basis.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller position:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (cl 11.1), described as "adequate." The DD-010 figure of AUD 180,000 is open, and the transfer of SOW3 project materials is conditional on payment (DD-004 cl 7.3). No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** The AUD 180k paid by the Seller before Completion (or deducted from price), a confirmatory IP assignment, and an uncapped specific indemnity for any Ironquay IP claims, not limited to the SOW3 fee amount.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; the indemnity as drafted does not cover the IP risk, and the transfer of title to project materials depends on the payment that is still outstanding.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller position:** The incident is "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter (item 6) states that the material does not establish unauthorised access, scope, or whether notification is required, and gives no loss amount. The file may contain about 1,240 records of personal information.
- **Buyer should want:** A forensic investigation report, confirmation of access and scope, and a determination under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breaches scheme. A specific indemnity for regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party costs, plus a warranty on privacy compliance and an escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** Require a specific indemnity and forensic evidence before signing. Urgently confirm whether an NDB assessment was started when the company became aware of the incident, since the 30-day assessment window may already have run.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller position:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs" (DD-008/DD-011; Disclosure Letter item 8). The disclosure does not say whether they are terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:** Copies of the renewal terms, confirmation of whether each is terminable, and an interim covenant requiring buyer consent to new or renewed contracts above a set threshold. Any accrued or committed amounts outside the ordinary course should be treated as debt-like.
- **Recommendation:** Require consent rights and disclosure of the terms; the "ordinary course" label does not establish whether the commitments reduce value post-Completion.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller position:** All claims fall under one general regime; the Seller's draft does not separate categories (cl 12, 13, 9.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes for (a) general warranties, (b) fundamental/title, (c) tax, (d) specific indemnities, and (e) fraud, each with its own cap, time limit, and threshold.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime; the risks in this deal differ in size and timing, and a single cap and time limit does not match that profile.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller position:** Title to 100% of shares is "evidenced by the share register" at DD-012, which identifies Harbourglass as the holder (Disclosure Letter item 10). The Seller notes that the buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:** An ASIC company extract and a register search, confirmation that the register matches ASIC records, sight of any share certificates, a PPSR search for encumbrances over the shares, confirmation of no options or convertibles, and a fundamental title warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent verification before signing; the Seller's register is not proof of title, and the buyer should not rely on the Seller's document alone.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller position:** The Seller considers tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" (Seller Update summary).
- **Buyer should want:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, with a time limit running to the statutory amendment period plus a buffer, and separate IP warranties (title, non-infringement, open source, and no encumbrances), with a specific indemnity covering the Ironquay matter.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; the tax and IP positions are not settled, and placing them under the general cap and time limit would leave the buyer exposed on the risks least likely to be discovered quickly.

---

**Key next steps for the deal team**
1. Make Bluefen consent and Riverlark payoff/discharge conditions precedent.
2. Move Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, Sandbar and the privacy incident into specific indemnities outside the general cap, with a retention or escrow.
3. Confirm the privacy incident status and NDB assessment timing immediately.
4. Verify title independently (ASIC and PPSR searches) before signing.
5. Have NSW counsel confirm the statutory rates and timelines cited above (payroll tax, super, Privacy Act, limitation periods) before they are used in negotiation.
